package.title: Economic Scarcity as Value: A Universal Framework for Blockchain and Beyond
package.data_as_of: Market capitalisations, issuance rates and user counts as of 5 August 2025.
package.units: Market value V and implied desirability D are in US dollars (the headline list converts D to trillions). The scarcity index S, its coefficient kappa and the five component scores lie between 0 and 1. The inflation rate pi is a fraction a year. User counts u are in units; u_tilde is u divided by one million.

licence.condition: Reuse of the results is allowed with credit to the paper.
licence.third_party_data: The inputs are market capitalisations from CoinGecko, issuance rates from StakingRewards.com, address counts from Glassnode, Etherscan and BitInfoCharts, and Bittensor participation counts from Taostats. Each row of data/inputs_2025-08.csv carries its source and access date. They remain the property of their sources and are not covered by the licence above.

headline.what: Implied desirability D of Bitcoin, baseline
Implied desirability D of Ethereum, baseline
Implied desirability D of Bittensor, at the baseline user count
headline.unit: trillion US dollars (it ranges widely with the user count)

headline.what: Share of 20,000 joint perturbations of the scores in which the ordering by S is unchanged

tables.what: Table 6: inflation, component scores, kappa and S by network.

columns.pi: annual inflation rate of the supply, a fraction
columns.G: governance mutability (1 where the rules are hardest to change)
columns.kappa: the structural coefficient, the average of the five scores
columns.S: the physical-scarcity index, kappa x (1 - pi)^beta, with beta 1.5 at the baseline

tables.what: Table 7: the baseline implied desirability by network.

columns.V_usd: market capitalisation on 5 August 2025, US dollars
columns.u: user count used at the baseline
columns.u_tilde: u divided by the common scale of one million
columns.D_usd: implied desirability, V / (S x u_tilde^alpha), US dollars

tables.what: D across alpha, beta and the Bittensor user range.

columns.beta: the sensitivity of S to inflation
columns.user_scenario: base, or low and high for Bittensor
columns.S: the scarcity index at that beta

tables.what: Perturbation of the component scores: how often the orderings by S and by D survive.

columns.delta: size of the shift applied to a score
columns.baseline_S_order: ordering of the networks by S at the baseline
columns.baseline_D_order: ordering by D at the baseline
columns.oat_S_flips: number of one-at-a-time shifts that change the ordering by S
columns.oat_D_flips: number that change the ordering by D
columns.mc_share_S_preserved: share of draws in which the ordering by S is unchanged
columns.mc_share_D_preserved: share in which the ordering by D is unchanged

tables.what: Each one-at-a-time shift of a score and the orderings it gives.

columns.network: the network whose score is moved
columns.component: the component moved: C, E, B, G or R
columns.shift: the shift applied, kept within 0 and 1
columns.S_order: ordering of the networks by S after the shift
columns.D_order: ordering by D after the shift
columns.S_order_changed: True if the ordering by S differs from the baseline
columns.D_order_changed: True if the ordering by D differs from the baseline

tables.what: kappa and S under other weights of the five components.

columns.scheme: equal, or 2x_C, 2x_E, 2x_B, 2x_G, 2x_R: the component whose weight is doubled
columns.kappa: the structural coefficient under that scheme
columns.S: the scarcity index under that scheme

tables.what: D with an n log n network effect in place of the power law: D = V / (S x (u / u0) x ln(1 + u)).

columns.user_scenario: base, or low and high for Bittensor
columns.D_nlogn_usd: implied desirability under this specification, US dollars; not comparable in level with the baseline D

tables.what: The ordering by D under different user scales, with one exponent for all networks and with protocol-specific exponents.

columns.spec: common_alpha: alpha = 2 for all; mixed_alpha: 2 for Bitcoin and Ethereum and 2.5 for Bittensor
columns.U0: the scale in which users are counted: 1, 1,000 or 1,000,000
columns.D_BTC: D of Bitcoin in US dollars with users counted in units of U0 (at U0 = 1,000,000 it is the baseline D). Only the ordering and the ratios within a row are meaningful
